findings.title: Run-id validation is duplicated in three places
findings.description: `finish._run_id` and `observe.RunObserver._observe_one` each check for a non-empty string `run_id`. `launch._text_parameter` repeats the check for `PARAM_RUN_ID`. Each raises its own `ValueError` with its own wording. The project's DRY rule says one place should own this, for example a single `run_id_of(entry)` helper. As written, a change to what counts as a valid id has to be made in three places.

findings.title: Tests lean on `type: ignore`, `Any` and `object` signatures, which conflicts with strict pyright
findings.description: The Python rules require strict pyright over `src` and `tests`, with zero errors. In the diff, `_hooked` returns `tuple[object, object]` and the caller then needs `# type: ignore[arg-type]`. `_arm_resolve_kill` monkeypatches `Store.journal_resolve` behind `# type: ignore[method-assign]`. Several test fixtures are typed `make_rig: Any`, and the fakes take `**kwargs: Any`. Typed callables, using the existing `PopenFactory` and `Callable[[str], RunPoll]`, would remove most of these suppressions.

findings.title: Test modules import private helpers from each other
findings.description: `test_budget_coverage` imports `_link` from `runner.test_probes` and suppresses the private-usage warning. `test_tenant.py` has its own `Rig` that duplicates `tick_support.Rig`. The shared setup should move into a support module such as `tick_support`. Otherwise one test file's refactor breaks another.

findings.title: `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` is a text-count guard
findings.description: The test counts the substring `except Exception` across the package, so it also matches comments and docstrings, and misses `except BaseException` and aliases. It enforces the rule loosely. The `BLE` ruff rule already enforces it mechanically, so an AST-based check or a reliance on `ruff` would be sturdier. Because the intent is a process-boundary catch, the `# noqa: BLE001` there is acceptable: it is justified by a comment and logs with `logger.exception`.

findings.title: `faults.py` module docstring is stale
findings.description: The docstring still says "Escalation writes join this module in a later task", but this diff adds `escalate` and `raise_expected_faults` to the same file. The sentence should be removed.

findings.title: `observe.py` exceeds the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: At 326 lines, the file is slightly over the guideline. The confirmed and unconfirmed observation paths could split into separate modules if it grows further in slices 123 to 126.

findings.title: `validate_settings` reads fields by string name
findings.description: `getattr(settings, name)` with a tuple of names defeats type checking, because a renamed field fails at runtime instead of in pyright. Direct attribute access in a short loop over `(label, value)` pairs would keep it checked.

findings.title: Process-boundary handling, budget discipline and crash ordering look sound
findings.description:
- **Exception handling:** Store failures and `UpstreamShapeError` re-raise. Anything else is logged with `logger.exception` and escalated. Expected faults are returned as values, not swallowed.
- **Subprocess budget:** Every subprocess call site (`poll`, the `cf` probes, `Popen`) checks `TickBudget.allows_call` first, and `test_budget_coverage` guards this.
- **Crash ordering:** The journal entry is written before launch. Finish records "block, then resolve" idempotently. The SIGKILL tests cover each crash point.
- **Import boundaries:** Rules 10 and 11 in `test_import_boundaries.py` keep the runner package's public surface narrow.

structured_findings.summary: Run-id validation is duplicated in three places
Tests lean on `type: ignore`, `Any` and `object` signatures, which conflicts with strict pyright
Test modules import private helpers from each other
Process-boundary handling, budget discipline and crash ordering look sound
